text: The sweep was executed LOCALLY (24-core workstation, 62 GB) with analysis/baselines/run_sweep.py rather than on CHTC: the pilot showed every method finishes a dataset in minutes, not hours, so the CHTC kit (chtc/make_baselines_manifest.py, baselines.sub, baselines_job.sh, baselines_one.py, collect_baselines.py; one job per (dataset, method)) is provided and tested for manifest generation but was not submitted. Phase 1 ran every method except the GLMCC delay probe (glmcc_d14) with 5 worker processes x 4 BLAS threads; phase 2 ran glmcc_d14 alone. Staging followed the protocol: (1) the accumulator reproduced the shipped glm_connectivity_sum4_5ms.npz bit-for-bit (test_accumulate.py); (2) the delay-recovery gate was run for every method on sweep_c50_seed01/normal at n = 50; (3) Tier 1 + Tier 2 were run on the quietest and the burstiest network (sweep_c40_seed12, sweep_c40_seed14) in both states and both arms at n = 50 (metrics_pilot_n050.csv) and the ordering inspected; (4) the full sweep at n = 200. Phase 1 finished in 5.6 h wall (40/40 jobs, 0 failed); phase 2 (glmcc_d14) ran afterwards on 2 + 3 workers.
projected: Measured on sweep_c50_seed01/normal at n = 50 before launch (4 BLAS threads, other jobs running), then scaled: the shared 1 ms pass (session load + 51 lag products) ~5 s at n = 50 -> ~20 s at n = 200 (linear in data); ccg_classical / fncch / tspe add ~1-3 s of per-pair work on top of it; ccg_jitter ~10 s at n = 50 (8 surrogate lag-product passes) -> ~40 s; glm_ridge ~25 s at n = 50 (fit + 8 surrogate fits) -> ~90 s; transfer entropy 28 s (1 ms), 15 s (2 ms), ~5 s (5, 10 ms) at n = 50 -> ~4x; stg ~13 s score + 7 s label-free (per-pair FFTs, independent of n); glmcc 0.31 s per 1000 unordered pairs = 157 s per dataset-arm at N = 926 (Newton on 428k pairs x 4 delays, 12.8 iterations per pair on average; per-pair cost independent of n), i.e. ~3.5 CPU-h for the 80 (dataset, arm) jobs; glmcc_d14 ~3.5x that (14 delays, warm-started) ~ 9 min per dataset-arm, ~12 CPU-h. Whole phase 1 projected at ~25-35 min per (session, state) job (seizure slower: 6x the spikes), 40 jobs -> ~20 CPU-h, ~4 h wall on 5 workers. Memory per worker projected < 4 GB (seizure-state jitter surrogates dominate).
spent: Phase 1 (every method except glmcc_d14; 40 (session, state) jobs x 14 methods x 2 arms, n = 200): 5.6 h wall on 5 workers x 4 threads, 0 failures. Normal-state jobs took 8-18 min, seizure-state jobs 41-86 min: the shipped GLM's 8 surrogate refits dominate there (e.g. sweep_c50_seed01/seizure: glm_ridge 1915 s, ccg_jitter 450 s, ccg_classical 303 s, te_1ms 213 s, glmcc 146 s, everything else < 60 s), because the sparse Gram assembly scales with the six-fold spike count. Per-method wall times for every job are in compute.json.
